description.narrative: Long term environmental sustainability and resilience of food production systems in the 2021-2025 CPD as aligned to NDPIII

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

Goal: to improve food security by addressing the environmental drivers of food insecurity and their root causes in Karamoja sub-region. Target: A 25% reduction in the number of households suffering from moderate or severe hunger, among which 35% are female headed households, by end of project.
Objective: To contribute to enhancing long-term environmental sustainability and resilience of food production systems in the Karamoja Sub-Region Target: A 20% increase in productivity of maize, sorghum, cassava andsweet potato, vegetables andbeans, in 1,800 hectares by end of project Target: A 15% increase in cattle and small stock productivity (milk/meat/eggs), by end of project.
OUTCOME 1: Supportive policies and incentives in place at district level to support improved crop and livestock production, food value-chains and INRM. Target: At least 1 policy or 1 incentive in force to support viable SLM/INRM approaches and related food value chains at landscape level in each selected site, by end of project.
Output 1.1: Operational multistakeholder platforms are supporting INRM at district and regional levels Target: At least 1 multi-stakeholder platform per district, supporting INRM, within which at least 30% are women, 30% are men, 20% are youth, and as appropriate 10% are indigenous people to represent communities, by end of project. One operational and comprehensive regional multistakeholder platform that includes meaningful participation by NGOs, private sector, CBOs, CSOs Government and development partners and that is linked to district level platforms, by end of project.
Output 1.2: Adequate legal instruments enabling INRM, land use planning and enforcement in place. Target: At least one INRM-enabling legal instrument, policy or by-law under implementation in each district by end of project.
OUTCOME 2: Increased land area under integrated natural resources management (INRM) and SLM practices for a more productive Karamoja landscape. Target: 450 ha of cropland, 180 ha of rangeland and 600 ha of forests per district are under INRM / SLM systems, by end of project (4,920 ha in total).
Output 2.1: Institutional technical capacities are strengthened to implement INRM/SLM. Target: Not Applicable in 2022
Output 2.2: Increase in the number of community members trained in INRM/SLM techniques Target: 12,000 community members trained in integrated natural resources management and SLM, among which half are women by end of project.
Output 2.3: Community groups are benefiting from income-generating activities (IGAs) introduced by the project. Target: At least 2500 community members, of which at least 60% are women, participate in alternative livelihoods schemes and small grant projects addressing SLM/INRM in the broader Karamoja landscape by end of project.
Output 2.4 Community level small grant projects in the Karamoja region that enhance ecosystem services, sustainable land management, innovate alternative livelihood options, are implemented. Target: 100% of grant amount disbursed by end of project, at least 50% of which is disbursed to women and youth groups.
OUTCOME 3. Framework in place for multi-scale assessment, monitoring and integration of resilience in production landscape and monitoring of GEBs . Target: At least, medium level of available data on resilience and GEBs by the end of the project
Output 3.1: Assessment and Monitoring of GEBs from project interventions Target: Three statistically representative M&E exercises conducted and changes analyzed (baseline, mid-term and end of project assessment and monitoring) over the duration of the project per selected landscape, by end of project
Output 3.2: Capacity in place to apply appropriate tools and practices for monitoring resilience at multiple scales. Target: At least 1 workshop held per year on monitoring resilience and building capacity for M&E, within the multi-stakeholder platform, among which 50% of participants are women.
Output 3.3. Project is linked to Regional Hub program for knowledge generation, exchange and dissemination. Target: At least 5 thematic knowledge products developed and shared at the regional meeting of the FSIAP programme countries and other platforms

Output 1.1: Operational multi-stakeholder platforms are supporting INRM at district and regional levels 1.1.2 Four multi stakeholder platforms formed around four product value chains at S/C Level. 1.1.3 Coherence for INRM and SLM across government policy, planning and decision-making processes and structures reviewed by NEMA. Recommendations for improved policy coherence at district level still under discussion. 1.1.4 28 District officials (53% women) per district trained on INRM and SLM and a gender analysis was done across the project area to inform MSP activities. 1.1.5 Success stories from grantees were documented and a project communication strategy was developed. 1.2.1 Legal frameworks on INRM/SLM are under review with support from Ministry of Justice and no training is yet conducted for policy makers and local leaders 1.2.2 35 CBLUPs and 8 SEAPs validated in a participatory exercise and a framework to align the PUPs with National Frameworks on rangelands is under development 1.2.4 A consulting firm has been contracted to conduct an assessment of the awareness on land rights and capacity building to address identified knowledge gaps in the communities. 2.4.1. 08 Community Based organizations received Small grants worth USD 72,000 and four(4) grant managers were contracted to disburse USD 480,000 to 28CBOs. Capacity building for the CBOs is on-going. 3.1.1 Test tools were developed for local landscape diagnosis types, severity, causes and effectiveness of SLM measures on the ecosystem and livelihoods. Tools are not pre-tested yet. 3.1.4 Training to govt technical and extension staff not yet trained 3.2.1 Participatory M&A not yet done 3.3.1 One presentation made to the regional hub platform, and a joint planning meeting was held with FAO, MAAIF and UNDP. Some stories were captured from the monitoring visit and lessons shall be disseminated after publication.
